minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved its outsourcing contract and adopted Leominster's new-connection sewer bank fee.
minutes.summary: The commission introduced its new contractor, Small Water Systems Services, and approved the contract effective August 1st. It acknowledged Leominster's sewer ordinance sections and adopted a one-time sewer bank fee on new connections matching Leominster's amount. It also approved an engineering quote for sewer extension applications and a 90-day amnesty for illegal connections. A builder's request for a water bill credit was held pending documentation.

votes.motion: Accept and execute the contract with Bruce and Debbie for outsourced sewer services
Acknowledge and recognize the Leominster sewer ordinance section 21-47-4-12
Acknowledge and recognize Leominster sewer ordinance 21.47.4.13
Implement Leominster ordinance 21-47-4-13 and adopt the sewer bank fee equal to Leominster's current amount, without automatic adjustment
Approve the fee for the PEF application for Sunset area and Pratt Street
Amnesty for illegal connections through October 31st
Approve the Weston Sampson contract with fixed hourly rate

budget_items.topic: Sewer bank surcharge on new connections
budget_items.what_was_said: Leominster's ordinance sets an upfront per-gallon surcharge on new users to fund infiltration and inflow work; Lunenburg is bound by its intermunicipal agreement.
The next step in finding infiltration sources was estimated as a costly investment.
A member noted connection fees were recently raised and argued for a lower bank fee; the board kept Leominster's amount.
Quotes were received for the Sunset extension alone and for Sunset plus Pratt Street combined.
Fines can be very high, with a policy minimum set for uniformity.
A builder sought forgiveness of a large bill from irrigation water used on a new lawn; the board asked for documentation.

decisions.decision: Amnesty period for illegal connections set at about 90 days, to be publicised by mailings and newspaper.
Builder's credit request held until he documents when the house closed; discussion of the 50 percent rule deferred.
A member will work with the administrator to find out how Leominster calculated its fee, with the rate to be revisited.
Next meeting set for the 13th of August at the DPW.

what_happened.line: The commission approved the outsourcing contract with Small Water Systems Services for sewer services, effective August 1st; the vote was unanimous.
The commission adopted a one-time sewer bank fee on new connections equal to Leominster's current amount, with no automatic adjustment; the vote was not audible.
The commission approved the fee for the engineering application covering the Sunset area and Pratt Street sewer extension.
An amnesty for illegal connections was set at about 90 days, to be publicised by mailings and newspaper; the vote was not audible.
A builder's request for credit on a large water bill was held until he documents when the house closed.

why_it_matters: New sewer connections will carry an upfront bank fee tied to Leominster's rate, a cost that lands on builders and new users and may reach home prices.
Owners with unpermitted sewer connections have a limited window to come forward before fines, which can be high, apply.

A member's follow-up with the administrator on how Leominster calculated its fee, after which the rate is to be revisited.
